title: Marathon Training Week 12: The 20 Miler That Broke Me
creator: Dani Okafor
description:
Week 12. Twenty miles. One very bad decision about breakfast.

Shoes and gear I mention (affiliate links - I earn a small commission at no cost to you):
https://www.runningwarehouse.com/?aff=danio

Strava: Dani Okafor
Plan I'm loosely following: Hal Higdon Intermediate 2
Race: Philadelphia Marathon, November

sentences.t: Okay, week twelve, and today was the big one.
Twenty miles, which is the longest I have ever run in my life.
I'm filming this about an hour after, so if I look a little dead behind the eyes, that's why.
Let me walk you through how it went, because it did not go to plan.
So I started at about six thirty, before it got hot.
First ten miles, honestly, amazing.
I was holding about a nine forty pace, feeling smooth, chatting to myself like a weirdo.
And then around mile eleven, my stomach just turned on me.
I'd tried a new breakfast this morning, which every single running book tells you not to do on a long run day.
Overnight oats with a ton of peanut butter.
Do not recommend.
So miles eleven through fourteen were a lot of walking and a lot of looking for bathrooms.
Weirdly, the one thing that didn't hurt at all was my feet.
I switched shoes about three weeks ago and I think it's made a real difference.
These have a really rockery sole and a ton of foam, so on the long stuff my calves aren't screaming anymore.
I'm not going to pretend I know the science, I just know my legs feel better the next day.
People always ask what shoes and gear I'm using, so I put it all on one page, it's in the description.
Heads up, those are affiliate links through Running Warehouse, so if you order through them I get a small commission.
It doesn't change the price for you, and I only put stuff on there that I've actually run in.
Anyway, back to the run.
Around mile fifteen I finally got my stomach back and started actually running again.
I took a gel at fifteen and another one at eighteen, and that last stretch felt surprisingly okay.
Not fast, but okay.
The last mile I had a little cheering section, which was my roommate on a bike yelling at me.
Very supportive, mostly.
Final time was three hours and twenty-eight minutes, which is way slower than my plan said.
But my coach texted me after and said, and I quote, you finished, that's the workout.
And I think that's right.
The point of the twenty miler isn't the pace, it's getting your body used to being out there that long.
So, lessons from today.
One, never try a new breakfast on a long run, I have learned this the hard way.
Two, start fueling earlier than you think, I should have taken a gel at mile eight.
Three, recovery is part of the run.
I've got a big bowl of rice and eggs waiting, and then I'm going to lie on the floor with my legs up the wall for twenty minutes.
Next week is a step back week, so the long run drops to fourteen, which honestly sounds like a vacation right now.
Race day is five weeks out, and I'm nervous, but I'm excited.
If you're training for something right now, tell me what it is in the comments, I love reading those.
Okay, I'm going to go eat everything in my kitchen.
See you next week.
